paper_context.research_question: How can macro and micro discourse structures be unified to better represent and analyze discourse organization, particularly the primary-secondary relationships at both levels, and how can this unified framework support automatic discourse analysis tasks?
main_claims: Primary-secondary relationships in discourse have been neglected as an independent analytical task despite their importance for discourse understanding and NLP applications

Micro-level discourse structure (rhetorical relations, logical semantics) and macro-level discourse structure (schematic structure, pragmatic function) can be unified into a single coherent representation framework
A macro-micro unified schema should combine RST-style rhetorical analysis at the sentence/clause level with schematic structure analysis at the paragraph/document level
Paragraph-level leaf nodes are appropriate units for macro-level discourse analysis, distinct from EDU-level micro analysis
Primary-secondary relationships exhibit strong dependence on discourse relation types, enabling predictive modeling
The proposed Macro Chinese Discourse Treebank (MCDTB) with 97 annotated news articles demonstrates the feasibility and utility of the unified schema
expected_evaluation_dimensions: Clarity and coherence of the unified macro-micro representation schema relative to existing theories (RST, Van Dijk macrostructure, schematic structure)
Annotation consistency and inter-annotator agreement on primary-secondary relations and discourse relations (reported: 20 documents with agreement/kappa metrics)
Corpus quality and statistical properties (533 paragraphs, 438 relations, distribution across relation types)
Task performance on discourse relation recognition (F-scores: 57.1%–66.7% on main types)
Task performance on primary-secondary relation recognition (F-scores: 50.0%–88.9% across three types)
Generalizability beyond news genre (acknowledged limitation: corpus limited to Xinhua news)
Practical utility for downstream NLP applications (summarization, translation, QA, IE, sentiment analysis)
Comparison with existing discourse treebanks (CDTB, RST-DT, PDTB) in terms of scope and annotation depth
Adequacy of feature engineering for classification tasks (text structure, content, semantic, relation structure features)

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: This paper proposes a unified macro-micro discourse structure representation schema for Chinese news discourse, combining RST-style micro-level rhetorical analysis with schematic structure macro-level analysis. The core contribution is treating primary-secondary relationships as an independent analytical task at both levels and demonstrating feasibility through a 97-article annotated corpus (MCDTB). The logical argument chain is: (1) primary-secondary relationships are neglected in discourse analysis despite importance for NLP applications; (2) micro and macro structures can be unified; (3) paragraph-level leaf nodes are appropriate for macro analysis; (4) primary-secondary relationships depend on discourse relation types; (5) MCDTB demonstrates feasibility; (6) preliminary experiments validate the schema. The paper's reasoning strengthens through concrete corpus construction and empirical validation but weakens in theoretical justification for unification, generalizability claims, and baseline comparisons. Section continuity is generally sound (Introduction→Related Work→Schema→Corpus→Experiments→Conclusion), but claim-to-evidence linkage exhibits gaps: the 'neglect' claim lacks systematic literature review; unification is presented as design choice rather than necessity; and utility for downstream tasks is claimed but not empirically demonstrated.
logical_argument_graph: Primary-secondary relationships are critical for NLP applications (MT, summarization, QA, IE, sentiment analysis) → currently treated as dispensable in discourse analysis → recognition has become a bottleneck
Existing theories focus on either micro (RST, logical semantics) or macro (Van Dijk, pragmatics) but not both → unification needed → propose unified schema combining both levels

Micro level: rhetorical relations between EDUs (logical semantic perspective) → Macro level: schematic structure between paragraphs (pragmatic function perspective) → both use primary-secondary relationships
Paragraph-level units are natural discourse segmentation → appropriate as leaf nodes for macro analysis → distinct from EDU-level micro analysis
Discourse relation types show strong dependence on primary-secondary relationship types (Table 6: Joint→MP, Elaboration→P-S, Background→P-S) → enables predictive modeling
Unified schema is operationalized in MCDTB: 97 articles, 533 paragraphs, 438 relations → demonstrates feasibility of annotation

Preliminary classification experiments on discourse relation recognition (F: 57.1%-66.7%) and primary-secondary relation recognition (F: 50.0%-88.9%) → validates schema appropriateness for discourse structure analysis tasks
Conclusion: macro-micro unified representation schema is effective for discourse structure analysis and supports downstream NLP applications

concerns.title: Unification of micro and macro structures presented as design choice rather than necessity
concerns.description: The paper proposes unifying micro-level (rhetorical, logical semantic) and macro-level (schematic, pragmatic function) discourse structures, but does not provide theoretical justification for why unification is necessary or superior to separate analyses. The unification appears to be a design choice rather than a principled requirement.

(2) Does unified representation enable better feature engineering or prediction? (3) Compare unified model with separate micro/macro models on downstream tasks to demonstrate added value.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: This paper proposes a unified macro-micro discourse representation schema for Chinese news discourse, combining RST-style micro-level rhetorical analysis with schematic structure macro-level analysis. The core contribution is treating primary-secondary relationships as an independent analytical task at both levels and demonstrating feasibility via a 97-article corpus (MCDTB) with preliminary classification experiments. The work is methodologically sound in schema design and corpus construction, but exhibits significant gaps in reproducibility, baseline comparisons, and empirical validation of core claims. The unification framework is presented as a design choice rather than theoretically justified necessity. Experimental validation is preliminary (maximum entropy classifier, no comparison with existing discourse parsers) and limited to news genre. Inter-annotator agreement metrics are referenced but not fully reported. The claim that primary-secondary relationships are 'neglected' lacks systematic literature review support. Paragraph-level granularity for macro analysis is asserted but not empirically validated against alternatives. The dependence between discourse relation types and primary-secondary relationships is observed but causal mechanisms unexplained. Downstream task utility (summarization, MT, QA, IE, sentiment analysis) is claimed in introduction but not empirically demonstrated.

strengths.title: Comprehensive corpus construction with detailed annotation
strengths.description: The MCDTB corpus includes 97 news articles with 533 paragraphs and 438 discourse relations, annotated for both micro-level rhetorical structure and macro-level schematic structure. The annotation strategy (top-down and bottom-up) is well-motivated and the corpus statistics are clearly reported.
evidence: Table 5 provides detailed corpus statistics: 97 documents, 533 paragraphs, 438 relations, 1339 sentences
Section 4.2 describes annotation strategy with clear rationale
Section 4.3 reports quality assurance measures (inter-annotator agreement on 20 documents)
Concrete examples (chtb_0019, chtb_0596) illustrate annotation in practice

strengths.title: Systematic treatment of primary-secondary relationships at both micro and macro levels
strengths.description: The paper explicitly defines three types of primary-secondary relationships (P-S, S-P, MP) and applies them consistently at both micro (sentence/clause level) and macro (paragraph/document level) levels. This systematic approach provides a unified perspective on discourse organization.
evidence: Section 3.3 provides clear definitions of three primary-secondary relationship types
Table 6 shows distribution of primary-secondary relationships across discourse relation types
Examples (chtb_0019 in Figure 7) demonstrate application of primary-secondary relationships in discourse trees

strengths.title: Empirical observation of strong dependence between relation types and primary-secondary relationships
strengths.description: Table 6 reveals a clear pattern: Joint relations are always multi-primary, Elaboration and Background are always P-S, Supplement is always P-S. This systematic dependence suggests that primary-secondary relationships may be predictable from discourse relation types, enabling classification-based approaches.
evidence: Table 6 shows perfect or near-perfect dependence patterns across relation types
Line 655 explicitly states: 'the relationship between discourse relation and primary-secondary relation is strong dependence'
This pattern enables the classification experiments in Section 5

strengths.title: Practical demonstration of schema applicability to news discourse
strengths.description: The successful annotation of 97 news articles demonstrates that the unified schema can be practically applied to a real discourse genre. The concrete examples (Figures 5-7) show how the schema captures both rhetorical and schematic structure in actual news articles.
evidence: 97 articles successfully annotated with both micro and macro structure
Figures 5-7 provide concrete examples of schema application to real news articles
Section 4.1 describes annotation process and principles (local and global principles)

strengths.title: Addresses underexplored aspect of discourse structure
strengths.description: The paper focuses on primary-secondary relationships as an independent analytical task, which appears to be underexplored in existing discourse structure research. This focus on a specific aspect of discourse organization that has received limited attention could provide value to the discourse analysis community.
evidence: Introduction (lines 101-107) motivates the importance of primary-secondary relationships
Related work (Section 2) shows that macro-level discourse analysis is relatively underdeveloped compared to micro-level
The paper expands discourse analysis from intra-paragraph to overall discourse level

concerns.title: Inter-annotator agreement metrics not fully reported
concerns.description: Table 4 is referenced multiple times (lines 648-650, 650) as containing inter-annotator agreement and kappa values, but the actual metrics are not shown in the provided text. This is critical for validating annotation quality and corpus reliability. Without these values, it is impossible to assess whether the 20-document sample demonstrates sufficient agreement to validate the 97-document corpus.
evidence: Line 648-650: 'we adopt the annotator consistency using agreement and kappa on 20 documents(chtb 0011-chtb 0030)'
Line 650: 'Table 4 illustrates the annotation consistency in detail'
Section 4.3 states: 'Its very difficult to achieve high consistence because the judgments of relation and structure are very subjective'
No actual agreement/kappa values provided in text
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Report inter-annotator agreement metrics (Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa, or Krippendorff's alpha) for discourse relations, primary-secondary relationships, and schematic structure. Specify which metric was used, how many annotators, and whether agreement was measured at leaf node level only or all levels. Provide separate metrics for each relation type to identify problematic categories.

concerns.title: No baseline or comparison with existing discourse parsing approaches
concerns.description: The experimental section (Section 5) reports classification results for discourse relation recognition (F: 57.1%-66.7%) and primary-secondary relation recognition (F: 50.0%-88.9%), but provides no comparison with existing discourse parsing systems or baselines. Related work (Section 2.2) mentions SPADE, HILDA, and Joty et al. (2013) with their performance on RST-DT, but no comparison is made. Without baselines, it is impossible to assess whether the reported performance is competitive or represents a meaningful contribution.
evidence: Section 5 reports F-scores in Tables 8-9 without any baseline comparison
Section 2.2 mentions prior work (SPADE, HILDA, Joty et al.) with performance metrics but no comparison is made
Line 751-752: 'All our classifiers are trained using nltk package with default parameters, and experimented with maximum entropy classifier' (no justification for classifier choice)
No comparison with CDTB (existing Chinese discourse treebank) results
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Implement or adapt existing discourse parsing approaches (HILDA, CRF-based parsers, neural parsers) as baselines on MCDTB. Compare maximum entropy classifier with SVM, CRF, and neural network baselines. If possible, compare with results on CDTB or other Chinese discourse corpora. Report performance on the same test set to enable fair comparison. Include ablation studies showing impact of different feature sets.

concerns.title: Resampling strategy may inflate reported performance estimates
concerns.description: The paper addresses class imbalance by resampling the minority class (S-P, Multi-Primary) to 10x the majority class (P-S). This resampling is applied before cross-validation, which can lead to inflated performance estimates because the test set will not reflect the natural class distribution. The paper does not report performance on the original imbalanced distribution or discuss the impact of resampling on generalizability.
evidence: Line 750-751: 'We solve the imbalance data problem of primary-secondary relation recognition by resampling strategy, that is, re-sampling the data set of nucleus in latter to ten times'
Table 6 shows severe imbalance: P-S (242), S-P (20), MP (176)
No analysis of resampling impact on performance estimates
No comparison with alternative imbalance handling methods (cost-sensitive learning, threshold adjustment, SMOTE)
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Report performance on both resampled and original (imbalanced) test sets. Use stratified cross-validation to ensure each fold maintains the original class distribution. Consider alternative imbalance handling methods: cost-sensitive learning (assign higher misclassification cost to minority class), threshold adjustment, or SMOTE. Analyze how resampling affects precision/recall trade-off for each class. Report macro-averaged F-score (unweighted average across classes) in addition to micro-averaged F-score.

concerns.title: Feature engineering is basic and lacks justification
concerns.description: Table 7 lists features used in classification experiments: text structural (number of paragraphs), text content (TF-IDF word pairs, first three words and POSs), semantic (similarity to title), and relation structure (hierarchical characteristics, position). These features are relatively basic and lack justification. No ablation study is provided to assess feature importance. No comparison with discourse-specific features (discourse connectives, coreference chains, syntactic structure) that might be more informative.
evidence: Table 7 lists features: text structural, text content, semantic, relation structure features
No ablation study or feature importance analysis provided
No justification for feature selection or comparison with alternative feature sets
No use of discourse-specific features (connectives, coreference, syntax) that are standard in discourse parsing
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Conduct ablation study removing each feature group (text structural, content, semantic, relation structure) and report impact on F-score. Analyze feature importance using permutation importance or SHAP values. Add discourse-specific features: discourse connectives (presence/type), coreference chains, syntactic structure (dependency/constituency), and rhetorical relation types. Compare performance with and without these features. Justify feature selection based on linguistic theory or prior work.

concerns.title: Paragraph-level granularity not empirically validated
concerns.description: The paper asserts that paragraph-level units are appropriate for macro-level discourse analysis (Section 3.1), but provides no empirical validation. No comparison is made with alternative granularities (sentences, discourse segments, rhetorical units). The appropriateness is justified only by the fact that paragraphs are 'natural segmented in the discourses' (line 352), which is a weak argument that may not generalize to genres with different paragraph conventions.
evidence: Section 3.1 states: 'we directly treat the paragraphs which are natural segmented in the discourses as leaf nodes'
No comparison with alternative leaf node definitions
No ablation study comparing paragraph-level with sentence-level or other granularities
No analysis of whether paragraph boundaries align with discourse-functional units
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Conduct ablation study comparing paragraph-level leaf nodes with alternative granularities: (1) sentence-level, (2) discourse segments defined by rhetorical structure, (3) discourse segments defined by schematic structure. For each granularity, report inter-annotator agreement and classification performance. Analyze alignment between paragraph boundaries and rhetorical/schematic structure boundaries. Discuss implications for generalization to non-news genres.

concerns.title: Dependence between relation types and primary-secondary relationships not statistically tested
concerns.description: The paper observes that discourse relation types strongly predict primary-secondary relationship types (Table 6), but does not provide statistical tests of independence (chi-square test, contingency table analysis). The dependence may be an artifact of the annotation scheme if annotators used relation type to infer primary-secondary relationships. No analysis is provided of whether this dependence is a linguistic universal or corpus-specific pattern.
evidence: Table 6 shows distribution of primary-secondary relationships by relation type
Line 655: 'the relationship between discourse relation and primary-secondary relation is strong dependence'
No chi-square test or statistical independence test provided
No analysis of whether dependence is linguistic universal or annotation artifact
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Conduct chi-square test of independence between discourse relation type and primary-secondary relationship type. Report test statistic, p-value, and effect size (Cramér's V). Analyze exceptions and counter-examples to the dependence pattern. Conduct cross-corpus validation on CDTB or other Chinese discourse corpora to assess whether dependence is universal or corpus-specific. Examine annotation guidelines to determine whether annotators were instructed to use relation type to infer primary-secondary relationships.

concerns.title: Unification of micro and macro structures not theoretically justified
concerns.description: The paper proposes to unify micro-level (rhetorical, semantic) and macro-level (schematic, pragmatic) discourse structures into a single representation, but does not provide theoretical justification for this unification. The unification is presented as a design choice rather than a necessity. No comparison is made with alternative approaches (separate micro/macro models, hierarchical models, or other unification schemes). It is unclear whether the unified representation adds explanatory power or enables better performance than separate analyses.
evidence: Introduction (lines 108-120) proposes unification without theoretical justification
Section 3 presents unification as design choice: 'we unify the primary-secondary relationship which defined in RST (nuclearity) and macrostructure separately'
No comparison with alternative unification approaches
No evidence that unified representation enables better performance than separate models
Relationship between RST nuclearity (relation-specific) and macro primary-secondary (discourse-global) not formally defined
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide theoretical justification for unification based on discourse theory (e.g., how RST nuclearity relates to discourse-level primary-secondary relationships). Compare unified schema with alternative approaches: (1) separate micro and macro models, (2) hierarchical model with micro structure nested within macro structure, (3) other unification schemes. Evaluate each approach on classification performance and downstream tasks. Formally define relationship between relation-specific nuclearity and discourse-global primary-secondary relationships.

concerns.title: Claimed utility for downstream tasks not empirically validated
concerns.description: The introduction (lines 095-100) motivates the work by citing applications in machine translation, summarization, question answering, information extraction, and sentiment analysis. However, the paper does not empirically validate utility on any of these downstream tasks. The evaluation is limited to intermediate tasks (discourse relation recognition, primary-secondary relation recognition) on the MCDTB corpus. Without downstream task evaluation, it is unclear whether the proposed schema actually improves performance on real applications.
evidence: Lines 095-100: 'the recognition of the discourse primary-secondary relationship not only helps to understand the discourse structure and semantics, but also provides strong support for deep natural language processing applications' (lists MT, summarization, QA, IE, sentiment analysis)
Section 5 evaluates only intermediate tasks (discourse relation recognition, primary-secondary relation recognition)
No evaluation on downstream tasks (summarization, MT, QA, IE, sentiment analysis)
Conclusion (lines 811-812): 'In the future work, we will enlarge the scale of the corpus and explore the various discourse patterns' (no mention of downstream task evaluation)
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Evaluate utility on at least one downstream task: (1) abstractive summarization (does primary-secondary information improve summary quality?), (2) machine translation (does discourse structure improve translation fluency?), (3) question answering (does discourse structure improve answer ranking?). For each task, compare performance with and without discourse structure information. Use automatic metrics (ROUGE for summarization, BLEU for MT, MRR for QA) and human evaluation if feasible.

concerns.title: Generalizability limited to news genre; no cross-genre evaluation
concerns.description: The corpus consists entirely of 97 Xinhua news articles. The paper does not evaluate whether the schema generalizes to other genres (academic papers, court documents, social media, fiction, etc.). News articles have conventional paragraph structure and schematic structure (summary-story pattern) that may not apply to other genres. The schema may require substantial revision for new genres, limiting its applicability.
evidence: Line 612: 'we annotate a Macro Chinese Discourse Treebank(MCDTB) consist of 97 Xinhua news wire articles'
Section 3 focuses on news schematic structure (Figure 3: summary-story pattern)
No evaluation on other genres
Conclusion (line 812): 'In the future work, we will enlarge the scale of the corpus and explore the various discourse patterns' (acknowledges limitation)
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Annotate sample documents from at least 2-3 other genres (academic papers, court documents, social media, fiction). Evaluate whether the schema applies without modification. If modifications are needed, document genre-specific constraints and variations. Conduct inter-annotator agreement study on each genre to assess schema clarity and applicability. Discuss how schematic structure varies across genres and implications for schema generalizability.

concerns.title: Corpus size modest compared to existing treebanks
concerns.description: The MCDTB corpus contains 97 documents with 533 paragraphs and 438 discourse relations. This is substantially smaller than existing discourse treebanks: RST-DT (~385 documents), PDTB (~2,312 documents), and CDTB (existing Chinese treebank, size not specified in paper). The small corpus size limits the reliability of performance estimates and may be insufficient for training robust machine learning models.
evidence: Table 5: 97 documents, 533 paragraphs, 438 relations
Section 2.2 mentions RST-DT and PDTB as major discourse corpora but does not compare corpus sizes
10-fold cross-validation on 97 documents yields ~10 documents per fold, which is small
No comparison with CDTB size or annotation depth
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Compare MCDTB size and annotation depth with CDTB, RST-DT, and PDTB. Discuss whether 97 documents is sufficient for reliable model training and evaluation. If feasible, expand corpus to at least 200-300 documents to improve statistical reliability. Report confidence intervals or bootstrap estimates of performance metrics to quantify uncertainty due to small corpus size.

concerns.title: Cross-validation strategy may yield unstable estimates
concerns.description: The paper uses 10-fold cross-validation on 97 documents (line 750), which results in ~10 documents per fold. With such small fold sizes, performance estimates may be highly variable and unstable. The paper does not mention stratified cross-validation, which would ensure that each fold maintains the original class distribution and relation type distribution.
evidence: Line 750: 'A 10 fold cross validation method is adopted'
97 documents / 10 folds = ~9.7 documents per fold
No mention of stratification by relation type or primary-secondary relationship type
No confidence intervals or variance estimates reported
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Use stratified k-fold cross-validation to ensure each fold maintains the original distribution of relation types and primary-secondary relationship types. Report confidence intervals (95% CI) or standard deviation of performance metrics across folds. Consider using leave-one-out cross-validation or repeated k-fold cross-validation to improve stability of estimates. Report both mean and variance of performance metrics.

concerns.title: Claim that primary-secondary relationships are 'neglected' lacks systematic evidence
concerns.description: The introduction claims that primary-secondary relationships are 'neglected' in discourse analysis (lines 101-107), but provides no systematic evidence. No literature review or citation count analysis is provided to support this claim. The claim relies on characterization of existing work rather than empirical analysis of prior research.
evidence: Lines 101-107: 'recognition of the discourse primary-secondary relationship has become the bottleneck in discourse structure analysis recently, largely due to the ignorance of its critical role'
No systematic literature review or citation count analysis
No comparison with prior work on nuclearity recognition or discourse structure analysis
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Conduct systematic literature review of discourse structure analysis work published in major venues (ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, COLING) over the past 10-15 years. Count citations to primary-secondary relationships, nuclearity, or related concepts. Identify papers that explicitly address primary-secondary relationships and papers that do not. Provide quantitative evidence (e.g., 'only 5% of discourse parsing papers explicitly address primary-secondary relationships') to support the 'neglected' claim.

concerns.title: Minority class performance suggests schema may not be equally appropriate for all relation types
concerns.description: Table 8 shows that Multi-Primary relation recognition achieves only 50.0% F-score (85.7% precision, 35.3% recall), substantially lower than P-S (79.3%) and S-P (88.9%). This suggests that the schema may not be equally appropriate for all primary-secondary relationship types. The low recall for Multi-Primary indicates that the classifier struggles to identify multi-primary relations, which may reflect ambiguity in the schema definition or insufficient training data.
evidence: Multi-Primary has high precision (85.7%) but low recall (35.3%), indicating under-prediction
Table 6 shows MP is the second most common type (176 out of 438 relations), so data imbalance is not the only issue
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Analyze errors in Multi-Primary relation recognition. Examine cases where the classifier fails to identify multi-primary relations (false negatives). Determine whether errors are due to: (1) ambiguous schema definition, (2) insufficient training data, (3) inadequate features, or (4) inherent difficulty of the task. Consider refining the schema definition for multi-primary relations or adding features that better distinguish multi-primary from P-S/S-P relations. Report error analysis and discuss implications for schema appropriateness.

comparable_works.citation_label: Aroyo & Welty (2015) - Truth Is a Lie: Crowd Truth and the Seven Myths of Human Annotation
comparable_works.relevance: Directly relevant to annotation quality and inter-annotator agreement methodology
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Aroyo & Welty argue that disagreement is signal, not noise, and that high agreement may indicate over-constrained guidelines rather than high-quality annotation. This is relevant to the paper's inter-annotator agreement evaluation (Section 4.3). The paper reports that 'it's very difficult to achieve high consistence because the judgments of relation and structure are very subjective' (line 650), which aligns with Aroyo & Welty's perspective. However, the paper does not report actual agreement metrics, making it impossible to assess whether the annotation quality is adequate.

comparable_works.citation_label: ARR Reviewer Guidelines - Check for common problems in NLP papers
comparable_works.relevance: Provides methodological standards for NLP papers, including corpus construction and evaluation
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: The ARR guidelines emphasize that published research should be 'technically sound and appropriately scoped' and flag common problems in NLP papers. The paper's evaluation methodology (maximum entropy classifier, no baseline comparison, limited downstream task evaluation) may fall short of these standards. The guidelines recommend comparing with existing approaches and providing comprehensive evaluation.

uncertainty_flags: Inter-annotator agreement values not fully reported in text; Table 4 referenced but metrics not shown
Claim that primary-secondary relationships are 'neglected' lacks systematic literature review evidence
Unification of micro and macro structures presented as design choice rather than theoretically justified necessity
Appropriateness of paragraph-level leaf nodes not empirically validated against alternative granularities
Dependence between discourse relation types and primary-secondary relationships observed but causal mechanism unexplained; no statistical test of independence
Corpus limited to news genre; generalizability to other genres unaddressed
Utility for downstream tasks (summarization, MT, QA, IE, sentiment analysis) claimed in introduction but not empirically validated
Baseline and comparison with existing discourse parsing approaches absent
Performance metrics lack context: unclear if competitive with prior work on RST-DT, PDTB, or CDTB
Imbalanced data handling via resampling may inflate reported scores; no analysis of impact on generalizability
Feature engineering (Table 7) is basic; unclear if schema enables better features than alternatives
Minority class performance (Multi-Primary: 50.0% F-score) suggests schema may not be equally appropriate for all relation types
Resampling strategy (10x minority class) may reduce generalizability to naturally imbalanced test data
10-fold cross-validation on 97 documents may yield unstable estimates; stratification not mentioned
Relationship between RST nuclearity (relation-specific) and macro primary-secondary (discourse-global) not formally defined
Corpus size (97 articles) modest compared to existing treebanks; statistical reliability of estimates unclear
No error analysis or qualitative evaluation of failure cases
Annotation guidelines not provided; unclear whether annotators were instructed to use relation type to infer primary-secondary relationships
alternative_interpretations: The strong dependence between discourse relation types and primary-secondary relationships (Table 6) may be an artifact of the annotation scheme rather than a linguistic universal. If annotators were instructed or implicitly encouraged to use relation type to infer primary-secondary relationships, the observed dependence would be tautological and not predictive of new data.

The modest performance on discourse relation recognition (F: 57.1%-66.7%) and primary-secondary relation recognition (F: 50.0%-88.9%) may reflect limitations of the feature engineering or classifier choice rather than limitations of the schema. Stronger classifiers (neural networks, structured prediction) or better features (discourse connectives, coreference, syntax) might yield substantially better results, suggesting the schema is sound but the experimental setup is limiting.

The unification of micro and macro structures may not add explanatory power beyond separate micro/macro analyses. The unified schema could be decomposed into separate micro and macro models without loss of information. The unification may be a convenient representation choice rather than a theoretical necessity.

The paragraph-level granularity for macro-level analysis may be specific to news genre and not generalizable to other genres. Academic papers, court documents, and social media may have different natural segmentation units (sections, paragraphs, posts) that do not align with news paragraph structure.

The claim that primary-secondary relationships are 'neglected' in discourse analysis may be overstated. Prior work on RST nuclearity, discourse parsing, and summarization may have implicitly addressed primary-secondary relationships without explicitly naming them. The paper may be reframing existing concepts rather than identifying a truly neglected aspect.

The corpus size (97 documents) may be insufficient for reliable model training and evaluation. Performance estimates may have high variance and may not generalize to larger corpora or other genres. The 10-fold cross-validation may yield unstable estimates due to small fold sizes.
transparency_notes: This review is based on the provided manuscript text and shared extraction stage. Inter-annotator agreement metrics (Table 4) are referenced but not shown in the provided text, limiting assessment of annotation quality.

The retrieved literature corpus (external Q1/Q2 articles) does not contain close matches to the paper's specific contribution (macro-micro unified discourse schema for Chinese news). This may reflect sparse coverage of discourse structure research in the retrieved corpus rather than lack of related work.
The reviewer guidelines retrieved emphasize technical soundness and appropriate scoping, which are relevant to assessing the paper's experimental methodology and evaluation comprehensiveness.

The paper's claims about 'neglected' primary-secondary relationships and 'strong dependence' between relation types and primary-secondary relationships are based on observations in the MCDTB corpus (97 documents) and may not generalize to other corpora or genres.

The paper's experimental evaluation is preliminary (maximum entropy classifier, no baseline comparison, limited downstream task evaluation) and may underestimate the potential of the proposed schema if stronger classifiers or better features are used.

The unification of micro and macro structures is presented as a design choice without explicit theoretical justification. The paper does not compare with alternative unification approaches or modular alternatives.

The paper's contribution is primarily methodological (schema design, corpus construction, preliminary experiments) rather than empirical (strong results on standard benchmarks) or theoretical (new discourse theory).

creativity_safeguard.novelty_not_validity_note: The paper's focus on primary-secondary relationships as an independent analytical task at both micro and macro levels appears to be novel. However, novelty should not be conflated with validity. The paper's core claims (primary-secondary relationships are neglected, micro-macro unification is beneficial, paragraph-level granularity is appropriate) require stronger empirical validation and theoretical justification. The lack of close analogs in the retrieved literature may reflect sparse coverage of discourse structure research in the corpus rather than genuine novelty.
counterfactual_conditions_for_success: If inter-annotator agreement metrics (Table 4) demonstrate high agreement (kappa > 0.70) on primary-secondary relationships and discourse relations, this would validate the annotation quality and support the corpus as a reliable resource.

If classification experiments with stronger baselines (SVM, CRF, neural networks) and better features (discourse connectives, coreference, syntax) yield substantially higher F-scores than the reported maximum entropy results, this would suggest the schema is sound but the experimental setup is limiting.

If the schema generalizes to non-news genres (academic papers, court documents, social media) with minimal modification, this would support the claim that the schema captures universal discourse organization principles rather than genre-specific patterns.

If downstream task evaluation (summarization, MT, QA, IE, sentiment analysis) demonstrates that discourse structure information improves performance, this would validate the claimed utility of the schema for NLP applications.

If statistical tests (chi-square test of independence) confirm that the dependence between discourse relation types and primary-secondary relationships is statistically significant and not due to chance, this would support the claim of strong dependence.

If comparison with existing discourse parsing approaches (HILDA, CRF-based parsers, neural parsers) shows that the proposed schema enables competitive or superior performance, this would validate the schema's appropriateness for discourse structure analysis tasks.

If the paper provides formal definitions of the relationship between RST nuclearity (relation-specific) and macro primary-secondary relationships (discourse-global), this would clarify the theoretical foundation of the unification.

novelty_lenses.verdict: Moderate incremental novelty with significant methodological gaps
novelty_lenses.rationale: The paper combines existing concepts (RST nuclearity, Van Dijk macrostructure, schematic structure) into a unified schema and applies them to Chinese news discourse. The focus on primary-secondary relationships as an independent task is a refinement of existing discourse analysis approaches rather than a fundamentally new perspective. The corpus construction is a useful resource but follows standard annotation practices. The experimental evaluation is preliminary and does not demonstrate clear advantages over existing approaches.
evidence: The schema combines RST (Mann & Thompson 1987), Van Dijk macrostructure (1980), and schematic structure (Van Dijk 2013) without substantial theoretical innovation
Primary-secondary relationships are related to RST nuclearity, which is well-established in discourse theory
The corpus construction follows standard annotation practices (inter-annotator agreement, top-down/bottom-up annotation strategy)
The experimental evaluation uses basic features and a simple classifier (maximum entropy) without comparison to existing approaches
uncertainty_flags: The novelty of treating primary-secondary relationships as an independent task is unclear; prior work on RST nuclearity may have implicitly addressed this aspect
The unification of micro and macro structures may be a convenient representation choice rather than a theoretical innovation
The corpus is limited to news genre; generalizability to other genres is unclear

novelty_lenses.verdict: Low disruptive novelty; unlikely to fundamentally change discourse analysis practice
novelty_lenses.rationale: The paper does not propose fundamentally new discourse theory or challenge existing paradigms. The unified schema is an extension of existing theories rather than a paradigm shift. The experimental results (F: 50.0%-88.9%) do not demonstrate clear advantages that would motivate adoption of the new schema over existing approaches. The corpus is limited to news genre and modest in size compared to existing treebanks. The paper is unlikely to have significant impact on discourse analysis practice unless downstream task evaluation demonstrates clear benefits.
evidence: The schema combines existing theories (RST, Van Dijk macrostructure, schematic structure) without proposing new theoretical foundations
The experimental evaluation is preliminary and does not compare with existing discourse parsing approaches
The corpus is limited to news genre (97 documents) and modest in size compared to RST-DT (~385 documents) and PDTB (~2,312 documents)
No downstream task evaluation demonstrates practical benefits of the proposed schema
The paper does not challenge or refute existing discourse analysis paradigms
uncertainty_flags: If downstream task evaluation demonstrates significant improvements (e.g., 5-10% improvement in summarization quality), the schema could have disruptive potential
If the schema generalizes to multiple genres and languages, it could become a standard framework for discourse analysis
If the paper's focus on primary-secondary relationships inspires new research directions in discourse analysis, it could have indirect disruptive impact

confidence_interval.rationale: The paper makes solid contributions in schema design and corpus construction, but exhibits significant methodological gaps that limit confidence in the reported results. The inter-annotator agreement metrics are not fully reported, baseline comparisons are absent, and downstream task utility is not validated. The experimental evaluation is preliminary and may underestimate the schema's potential if stronger classifiers or better features are used. The corpus is limited to news genre and modest in size. The theoretical justification for the unification is weak. These factors create substantial uncertainty about the validity and impact of the work. However, the paper addresses an underexplored aspect of discourse analysis (primary-secondary relationships) and demonstrates feasibility of the proposed schema through corpus construction and preliminary experiments. The work could be valuable if the methodological gaps are addressed in future revisions.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: This paper proposes a macro-micro unified discourse representation schema that integrates RST-style micro-level rhetorical analysis with macro-level schematic structure analysis, treating primary-secondary relationships as an independent analytical task. The contribution is framed as extending existing discourse theories (RST, Van Dijk macrostructure) by combining them into a single coherent framework and demonstrating feasibility through a corpus of 97 annotated Chinese news articles (MCDTB). From an incremental-contribution lens, the work exhibits moderate novelty: it reorganizes and formalizes existing theoretical concepts (RST nuclearity, schematic structure, pragmatic function) rather than introducing fundamentally new constructs. The unification itself is presented as a design choice rather than a theoretically justified necessity. The corpus contribution is meaningful but modest in scale. Preliminary experiments validate the schema's applicability but lack comparison with existing discourse parsing approaches, limiting assessment of whether the unified representation enables better performance or merely reorganizes existing knowledge. The work advances discourse analysis incrementally by foregrounding primary-secondary relationships and proposing a unified representation, but the innovation is primarily in schema design and corpus construction rather than in theoretical insight or methodological breakthrough.
logical_argument_graph: Primary-secondary relationships are underexplored in discourse analysis (C1) → Recognition of primary-secondary relationships should be an independent task (A1) → Unification of micro and macro structures can represent both simultaneously (C2)

Micro-level analysis operates at EDU/clause level; macro-level at paragraph level (A2) → Paragraph-level leaf nodes are appropriate for macro analysis (C3) → Corpus annotation using paragraphs as leaf nodes demonstrates feasibility (C5)

Micro structures involve logical semantics (RST); macro structures involve pragmatic function (schematic structure) (A3) → Unified schema combines both perspectives (C2) → Schematic structure is appropriate macro-level representation (A3)

Discourse relation types strongly predict primary-secondary relationship types (C4, Table 6) → Primary-secondary relationships exhibit dependence on relation types (C4) → Predictive modeling is enabled (C4)
MCDTB corpus with 97 articles demonstrates feasibility (C5) → Preliminary experiments show task performance (C6) → Schema is appropriate for discourse analysis tasks (C6)
News genre exhibits schematic structure patterns (Figure 3) → Schema is designed for news genre (A4) → Generalizability to other genres is unaddressed (A4)

identified_claims.claim_label: Primary-secondary relationships neglected in discourse analysis
identified_claims.claim_text: Recognition of the discourse primary-secondary relationship has become the bottleneck in discourse structure analysis recently, largely due to the ignorance of its critical role in discourse structure analysis by viewing it only as a dispensable component in the analysis of the discourse rhetorical structure.
evidence: Explicit statement that primary-secondary relationships are treated as dispensable in existing discourse analysis
Motivation citing applications in MT, summarization, QA, IE, sentiment analysis (lines 095-100)
Contrast with RST nuclearity which is relation-specific rather than discourse-global (lines 101-107)

Claim relies on characterization of existing work rather than systematic literature review
Unclear whether prior work explicitly dismissed or simply did not foreground this aspect

alternative_interpretations: The perfect dependence between relation types and primary-secondary relationships (Table 6) could reflect annotation guidelines that constrain primary-secondary relationships based on relation type, rather than capturing independent linguistic phenomena. This would suggest the dependence is an artifact of the annotation scheme rather than a linguistic universal.

The modest performance on primary-secondary relation recognition (F-scores 50.0%-88.9%) could indicate that the unified schema is not well-suited for this task, rather than validating the schema. The low performance on Multi-Primary class (50.0% F-score) suggests the schema may conflate distinct phenomena.

The lack of comparison with existing discourse parsers could mean either: (1) the unified schema enables better performance than existing approaches (but this is not demonstrated), or (2) the schema is not competitive with existing approaches (but this is not tested).

The corpus contribution could be viewed as incremental rather than novel: it extends CDTB with macro-level annotations rather than introducing fundamentally new annotation categories or theoretical insights.

The unification of micro and macro structures could be viewed as a convenient organizational choice rather than a theoretically justified necessity. Separate micro and macro models might be equally effective and more interpretable.

The paper's claim that primary-secondary relationships are 'neglected' could be overstated. Prior work may have implicitly captured these relationships through nuclearity or other mechanisms, even if not explicitly foregrounded.
transparency_notes: This review assesses novelty from an incremental-contribution lens, which emphasizes how the work extends, refines, or reorganizes existing paradigms. The paper exhibits moderate incremental novelty: it reorganizes existing theoretical concepts (RST, schematic structure) and formalizes primary-secondary relationships, but does not introduce fundamentally new constructs or theoretical insights.

The retrieved literature corpus did not return discourse-specific papers directly comparable to this work. The top-retrieved documents address annotation disagreement, passive syntax, and sentiment analysis—tangentially related but not directly comparable. This suggests either: (1) the paper addresses a relatively underexplored area (supporting innovation signal), or (2) the retrieval system did not find the most relevant prior work (limiting assessment of semantic overlap).
The shared extraction stage identified 10 key assumptions, several of which are implicit rather than explicit. This review has flagged these assumptions as sources of uncertainty and novelty risk.

This reviewer's role is to assess novelty, not to recommend accept/reject. The analysis identifies both strengths (foregrounding of primary-secondary relationships, comprehensive schema design, corpus resource) and concerns (lack of theoretical justification for unification, weak baselines, limited generalizability). The overall assessment is that the work makes a meaningful but incremental contribution to discourse analysis.

The paper's contribution is distributed across multiple dimensions: theoretical (unified schema), resource (MCDTB corpus), methodological (annotation guidelines), and empirical (preliminary experiments). Assessing novelty across these dimensions reveals that the theoretical contribution is modest (reorganization of existing concepts), the resource contribution is meaningful (dual-level annotation), and the empirical contribution is limited (weak baselines, no downstream validation).

The creativity safeguard analysis suggests the paper lacks close analogs in the retrieved literature, which could indicate innovation. However, the absence of close analogs could also reflect gaps in the retrieval system or the paper's positioning within a specialized subfield (Chinese discourse analysis).

creativity_safeguard.novelty_not_validity_note: The paper's lack of close analogs in the retrieved literature could indicate genuine innovation in unifying micro and macro discourse structures. However, the absence of analogs does not guarantee validity or impact. The work could be novel but not useful if: (1) the unification does not enable better downstream task performance, (2) the schema is too genre-specific to generalize, or (3) the annotation complexity outweighs the analytical benefits. Novelty and validity are orthogonal dimensions.
counterfactual_conditions_for_success: If the unified schema enables substantially better performance on downstream tasks (summarization, MT, QA, IE, sentiment analysis) compared to separate micro/macro models, the contribution would be more impactful.
If the paper demonstrates that paragraph-level granularity is optimal through ablation studies comparing alternative leaf node definitions, the schema design would be more principled.

If the paper provides formal theoretical justification for unifying RST nuclearity (relation-specific) with macro primary-secondary relationships (discourse-global), the contribution would be more coherent.
If the paper validates the schema on multiple genres (academic papers, court documents, social media) and identifies genre-specific constraints, the generalizability would be clearer.
If the paper compares with stronger baselines (SVM, neural networks, structured prediction) and existing discourse parsers, the empirical validation would be more convincing.

If the paper explains why perfect dependence between relation types and primary-secondary relationships (Table 6) reflects linguistic constraints rather than annotation artifacts, the empirical findings would be more credible.

If the paper demonstrates that the unified schema enables novel linguistic insights or enables new NLP applications not possible with separate micro/macro models, the theoretical contribution would be more substantial.

novelty_lenses.verdict: Moderate incremental novelty with meaningful but limited theoretical contribution
novelty_lenses.rationale: The paper reorganizes and formalizes existing theoretical concepts (RST, schematic structure, Van Dijk macrostructure) into a unified representation. This is a useful reorganization but not a fundamental theoretical innovation. The primary-secondary relationship is foregrounded as an independent task, which is a conceptual contribution. The corpus resource (MCDTB) is meaningful but modest in scale (97 articles). The empirical validation is weak (maximum entropy classifier, no baselines, no downstream tasks). Overall, the work extends existing paradigms incrementally rather than introducing new theoretical frameworks or methodological breakthroughs.

The primary-secondary relationship, while underexplored, is not a fundamentally new concept—it is implicit in RST nuclearity. confidence_interval.rationale: The assessment confidence is moderate-to-high for identifying specific concerns (weak baselines, limited generalizability, lack of downstream validation) but lower for assessing overall novelty and impact. The paper makes meaningful contributions in foregrounding primary-secondary relationships and proposing a unified schema, but the theoretical justification is weak and the empirical validation is limited. The work is clearly above the threshold of trivial contribution but below the threshold of significant innovation. The confidence interval reflects uncertainty about: (1) whether the unification is theoretically justified or merely convenient, (2) whether the schema enables better downstream task performance (not tested), (3) whether the perfect dependence in Table 6 reflects linguistic constraints or annotation artifacts, and (4) whether the work will have impact beyond the Chinese discourse analysis community. The upper bound (0.75) reflects the possibility that the work makes a meaningful incremental contribution that advances discourse analysis despite the methodological limitations.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: This paper proposes a macro-micro unified discourse structure representation schema that integrates primary-secondary relationship recognition across both micro-level (rhetorical/semantic) and macro-level (schematic/pragmatic) discourse analysis. The core novelty claim is that primary-secondary relationships have been neglected as an independent analytical task despite their importance, and that unifying micro and macro perspectives into a single coherent framework is both feasible and valuable. The authors construct the Macro Chinese Discourse Treebank (MCDTB) with 97 annotated news articles and demonstrate preliminary classification results. From a disruptive novelty lens, the work introduces a conceptual reframing of discourse structure analysis by: (1) elevating primary-secondary relationships from a byproduct of rhetorical analysis to an independent analytical focus; (2) proposing explicit unification of traditionally separate micro and macro discourse theories; (3) extending discourse analysis from intra-paragraph to document-level scope. However, the innovation signal is tempered by reliance on established theories (RST, Van Dijk macrostructure, schematic structure) and limited empirical validation of the unification's explanatory power. The work is coherent and addresses a genuine gap in discourse analysis practice, but the theoretical justification for unification remains implicit rather than formally argued.

Paragraph-level units are natural discourse segmentation boundaries in news genre → operationalizes macro-level leaf node definition
Discourse relation types exhibit strong statistical dependence on primary-secondary relationship types (Table 6) → enables predictive modeling and suggests non-arbitrary relationship
Unified schema can be instantiated in a corpus of 97 annotated news articles → demonstrates feasibility
Classification experiments on discourse relation and primary-secondary relation recognition achieve measurable F-scores → validates schema appropriateness for computational tasks
Unification of micro and macro perspectives within single representation → claimed to support discourse structure analysis but mechanism of benefit unclear

Figures 5-6 provide parallel macro and micro annotations for same document
Figure 7 demonstrates primary-secondary relationship annotation with arrow notation

concerns.title: Unification of micro and macro structures lacks formal theoretical justification

concerns.title: Paragraph-level granularity not empirically validated as optimal for macro analysis

No comparison with alternative leaf node definitions

Report agreement separately for each relation type. Discuss whether 20-document sample is representative of remaining 77 documents. concerns.title: Resampling strategy may inflate performance estimates and reduce generalizability
concerns.description: Section 5 addresses class imbalance by resampling minority class (S-P, MP) to 10x majority class (P-S). This strategy may inflate precision/recall estimates on test data and reduce generalizability to naturally imbalanced distributions.

Table 6 shows severe imbalance: P-S (242), S-P (20), MP (176); resampling S-P to 200 creates artificial balance
10-fold cross-validation on 97 documents with resampling may not reflect real-world imbalanced distributions
Assumption A8 identifies risk that resampling may reduce generalizability
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Compare resampling strategy with alternatives: (1) cost-sensitive learning (assign higher misclassification cost to minority class); (2) threshold adjustment (optimize decision boundary for minority class); (3) stratified cross-validation (ensure each fold maintains original class distribution). Report F-scores under both resampled and naturally imbalanced conditions. Discuss which strategy is more appropriate for downstream applications.

concerns.title: Baseline and comparative evaluation absent
concerns.description: The paper reports F-scores for discourse relation recognition (57.1%-66.7%) and primary-secondary relation recognition (50.0%-88.9%) but provides no baseline or comparison with existing discourse parsing approaches. Cannot assess if performance is competitive or above random.
evidence: Section 5 (lines 751-756) describes maximum entropy classifier with default parameters but no baseline comparison
No comparison with existing discourse parsers (SPADE, HILDA, Joty et al.) mentioned in Section 2.2
No comparison with simpler baselines (majority class, random, rule-based)
No comparison with stronger classifiers (SVM, neural networks, structured prediction)
Tables 8-9 report absolute F-scores without context or comparison
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Add baseline and comparative evaluation: (1) majority class baseline (always predict most frequent relation type); (2) rule-based baseline (predict primary-secondary type based on relation type from Table 6); (3) stronger classifiers (SVM, logistic regression, neural network); (4) comparison with existing discourse parsers if applicable. Report performance on same test set with same evaluation metrics. Discuss why proposed schema enables better/worse performance than alternatives.

concerns.title: Feature engineering is basic and not ablated
concerns.description: Table 7 lists four feature categories (text structural, text content, semantic, relation structure) but provides minimal detail and no ablation study. Unclear if features are sufficient or if schema enables better features than alternatives.
evidence: Table 7 lists features: text structural (number of paragraphs), text content (word pairs, words/POSs), semantic (semantic similarity to title), relation structure (hierarchical characteristics, position)
No feature importance analysis or ablation study
Features are generic; no discourse-specific features (connectives, coreference, syntax, discourse markers)
Assumption A7 identifies risk that feature engineering may be limiting factor
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Conduct ablation study removing each feature category and reporting F-score change. Add discourse-specific features: (1) discourse connectives and markers; (2) coreference chains; (3) syntactic structure; (4) lexical overlap. Report feature importance scores. Discuss whether unified schema enables better feature extraction than separate micro/macro models.

concerns.title: Small corpus size limits generalizability and statistical reliability
concerns.description: The MCDTB contains 97 articles (533 paragraphs, 438 relations), which is modest compared to existing treebanks (RST-DT ~385 documents, PDTB ~2,312 documents). 10-fold cross-validation on 97 documents yields folds of ~10 documents, which may produce unstable performance estimates.
evidence: Section 4.1 (line 612) states corpus consists of '97 Xinhua news wire articles'
Table 5 reports 533 paragraphs, 438 relations across 97 documents
Section 5 (line 750) states '10 fold cross validation method is adopted'
Fold size ~10 documents is small; high variance in fold composition may lead to unstable estimates
Comparison with existing treebanks shows MCDTB is substantially smaller
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Report cross-validation results with confidence intervals (standard deviation across folds). Conduct stratified cross-validation ensuring each fold maintains original class distribution and relation type distribution. Report performance separately for different document lengths/relation counts. Discuss minimum corpus size needed for reliable model training. Plan for corpus expansion to match scale of existing treebanks.

concerns.title: Downstream task utility claimed but not empirically validated
concerns.description: The introduction motivates the work by citing applications in MT, summarization, QA, IE, and sentiment analysis, but the paper does not empirically validate utility on any downstream task. Utility is inferred from intermediate task performance only.

Conclusion (line 801) claims 'recognition of the discourse primary-secondary relationship... provides strong support for deep natural language processing applications'
Section 5 evaluates only discourse relation and primary-secondary relation recognition; no downstream task evaluation
No evidence that improved discourse relation/primary-secondary recognition translates to improved summarization, MT, QA, IE, or sentiment analysis performance
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Select one downstream task (e.g., extractive summarization or sentiment analysis) and evaluate: (1) baseline system without discourse structure; (2) system with existing discourse structure (RST-DT or CDT); (3) system with proposed macro-micro unified structure. Report task-specific metrics (ROUGE for summarization, F1 for sentiment). Discuss whether unified schema provides additional benefit over existing approaches.

concerns.title: Genre-specificity of schema not addressed; generalizability unclear
concerns.description: The corpus is limited to Xinhua news articles, and the schematic structure (summary-story) is specific to news genre. No discussion of how schema applies to other genres (academic papers, court documents, social media, fiction).

concerns.actionable_suggestion: Discuss genre-specificity explicitly: (1) identify which schema components are news-specific (schematic structure, discourse relations, primary-secondary patterns); (2) propose modifications for other genres (academic papers: abstract-introduction-methods-results-discussion; court documents: claim-evidence-reasoning); (3) annotate sample documents from 2-3 other genres to test schema applicability; (4) report inter-annotator agreement and classification performance on non-news genres.

concerns.title: Dependence between relation types and primary-secondary categories may reflect annotation design rather than linguistic structure
concerns.description: Table 6 shows perfect or near-perfect correlation between certain relation types and primary-secondary categories (Joint→MP, Elaboration→P-S, Background→P-S). evidence: Table 6 shows: Joint (151 relations, all MP 100%); Elaboration (121, all P-S 100%); Background (47, all P-S 100%); Supplement (30, all P-S 100%)

concerns.title: Imbalanced class distribution not adequately addressed in analysis
concerns.description: Table 6 shows severe class imbalance (P-S: 242, S-P: 20, MP: 176). While resampling is applied during training, the analysis does not discuss implications for model generalization or discuss whether imbalance reflects linguistic reality or annotation artifact.

concerns.actionable_suggestion: Analyze imbalance sources: (1) is P-S genuinely more common in news discourse, or does annotation guideline bias toward P-S?; (2) compare imbalance distribution across relation types (Table 6 shows variation); (3) discuss whether resampling is appropriate or whether cost-sensitive learning better reflects linguistic reality; (4) report performance on naturally imbalanced test set (without resampling) to assess real-world applicability.

concerns.title: Claim that primary-secondary relationships are 'neglected' lacks systematic evidence
concerns.description: The paper claims primary-secondary relationships are 'neglected' in discourse analysis, but provides no systematic literature review, citation analysis, or evidence that prior work explicitly dismissed this aspect. The claim relies on characterization rather than quantitative evidence.

comparable_works.citation_label: Mann & Thompson (1987) - Rhetorical Structure Theory
comparable_works.relevance: Foundational micro-level discourse theory that defines nuclearity (nucleus vs. satellite) as relation-specific property. Paper proposes to extend nuclearity concept to discourse-global primary-secondary relationships.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: RST nuclearity is relation-specific (determined by rhetorical relation type); proposed primary-secondary is discourse-global (determined by overall discourse structure). Paper claims these are compatible but does not formally justify relationship.
comparable_works.source_trace: Referenced in Section 2.1 (lines 201-220); Introduction (lines 101-107) contrasts RST nuclearity with proposed primary-secondary approach

comparable_works.citation_label: Van Dijk (1980, 1985, 2013) - Macrostructure Theory
comparable_works.relevance: Foundational macro-level discourse theory that proposes hierarchical macrostructures representing global discourse coherence. Paper adopts Van Dijk's schematic structure (Figure 3) as basis for macro-level analysis.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Van Dijk focuses on semantic macrostructures; paper proposes pragmatic function-based schematic structures. Paper extends Van Dijk's framework to include primary-secondary relationships at macro level.
comparable_works.source_trace: Referenced in Section 2.1 (lines 201-220); Section 3 (lines 301-310) uses Van Dijk's schematic structure for news genre as primary example

comparable_works.citation_label: Li et al. (2014) - Connective-driven Dependency Tree (CDT)
comparable_works.relevance: Chinese discourse structure representation that uses EDUs as leaf nodes and connectives as non-leaf nodes. Paper builds on CDT for micro-level analysis and extends to macro level.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: CDT focuses on micro-level rhetorical structure; paper proposes unified micro-macro framework. Paper adopts CDT definition for micro-structure (Section 3, line 368) but extends with macro-level schematic structure.
comparable_works.source_trace: Referenced in Section 2.1 (lines 201-220); Section 3 (line 368) states 'For the microstructure, we follow the definition of CDT'

comparable_works.citation_label: Marcu (2000), Soricut & Marcu (2003), Hernault et al. (2010), Joty et al. (2013) - Discourse Parsing Systems
comparable_works.relevance: Existing discourse parsing systems that operate primarily at micro level (sentence/EDU level). Paper proposes macro-level parsing as complementary or alternative approach.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Existing systems focus on micro-level rhetorical structure parsing; paper proposes macro-level schematic structure parsing. No direct comparison of performance or applicability.
comparable_works.source_trace: Referenced in Section 2.2 (lines 275-299); Table 2 shows performance of existing systems on RST-DT corpus

comparable_works.citation_label: Martin & Rose (2003) - Super-theme Theory
comparable_works.relevance: Macro-level discourse theory focusing on thematic organization and pragmatic function. Paper cites as example of macro-level theory but does not deeply engage with framework.
comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Super-theme theory focuses on thematic progression; paper focuses on primary-secondary relationships and schematic structure. Limited overlap in theoretical focus.

The paper's claim that primary-secondary relationships are 'neglected' may be overstated. Prior discourse analysis work (RST, Van Dijk, CDT) may have implicitly addressed primary-secondary relationships through nuclearity or hierarchical structure, even if not explicitly labeled as such.

The unification of micro and macro structures may be a convenient design choice rather than a theoretically necessary integration. Separate micro and macro models might achieve equivalent or superior performance without the added complexity of unification.

The modest F-scores (57.1%-66.7% for discourse relations, 50.0%-88.9% for primary-secondary relations) may indicate that the schema is not sufficiently predictive or that the classification task is inherently difficult due to subjective annotation. Stronger baselines or feature engineering might reveal that performance is not competitive with existing approaches.

The corpus size (97 articles) may be insufficient for reliable model training and generalization. The observed patterns (especially the dependence in Table 6) may be artifacts of the small, genre-specific corpus and may not generalize to larger, more diverse datasets.

The paper's focus on news genre may reflect convenience rather than principled choice. The schema's applicability to other genres (academic papers, court documents, social media) remains unknown, limiting the generalizability of the contribution.
transparency_notes: This review applies a disruptive-thinking lens that protects unconventional ideas from being penalized merely for divergence from mainstream literature. The paper's core novelty—unifying micro and macro discourse structures and elevating primary-secondary relationships to independent analytical status—is conceptually coherent and addresses a genuine gap in discourse analysis practice.

However, the review also identifies significant methodological concerns (missing baselines, unreported inter-annotator agreement, resampling strategy, small corpus size) that are distinct from novelty risk. These methodological issues should be addressed regardless of whether the work is considered novel.

The paper's theoretical contribution (unification framework) is not strongly validated by the empirical work (classification experiments on intermediate tasks). The connection between theoretical novelty and empirical validation is weak, which limits confidence in the practical utility of the proposed framework.

The retrieved literature corpus did not contain close precedent for the specific framing of macro-micro unified discourse structure with primary-secondary relationships. This absence of precedent may indicate genuine innovation or may reflect limited coverage of Chinese discourse analysis in the external literature corpus.

The paper's treatment of primary-secondary relationships as independent from rhetorical structure analysis is a conceptual reframing that could be valuable if properly justified. However, the justification is implicit rather than explicit, and the relationship between relation-specific nuclearity (RST) and discourse-global primary-secondary relationships is not formally defined.

The empirical validation (classification experiments) uses simple maximum entropy classifiers and basic features, which may underestimate the schema's potential. Stronger classifiers and more sophisticated feature engineering might reveal greater utility of the unified framework.

The paper's contribution is best characterized as a resource contribution (MCDTB corpus) combined with a theoretical framework contribution (macro-micro unified schema). The resource contribution is concrete and valuable; the theoretical contribution is coherent but not strongly validated.

creativity_safeguard.novelty_not_validity_note: The paper's core innovation—unifying micro-level rhetorical/semantic analysis with macro-level schematic/pragmatic analysis into a single coherent framework, and elevating primary-secondary relationships to independent analytical status—lacks close analogs in the retrieved literature. counterfactual_conditions_for_success: If the paper formally justified why unification of micro and macro structures is theoretically necessary (not merely convenient), the contribution would be stronger. Currently, unification is presented as design choice without rigorous theoretical grounding.

If the paper empirically validated the unified schema on downstream tasks (summarization, MT, QA, IE, sentiment analysis) rather than only intermediate classification tasks, the practical utility would be demonstrated. Currently, utility is claimed but not validated.

If the paper compared the unified schema with alternative approaches (separate micro/macro models, hierarchical discourse parsing, other unification strategies), the relative merit of the proposed approach would be clearer. Currently, no comparative evaluation exists.

If the paper extended the framework beyond news genre and demonstrated applicability to other genres (academic papers, court documents, social media), the generalizability and broader impact would be established. Currently, applicability is limited to news.

If the paper provided stronger empirical validation with larger corpus (comparable to RST-DT or PDTB), more sophisticated classifiers, and comprehensive baselines, the practical viability of the approach would be more convincing. Currently, the corpus is small and evaluation is preliminary.

If the paper explicitly addressed whether the observed dependence between discourse relation types and primary-secondary categories reflects linguistic structure or annotation design, the validity of the core empirical observation would be clarified. Currently, this distinction is not addressed.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: This paper proposes a macro-micro unified discourse structure representation schema for Chinese news discourse, combining RST-style micro-level rhetorical analysis with schematic structure macro-level analysis. The core claims are: (1) primary-secondary relationships are neglected in discourse analysis despite importance for NLP applications; (2) micro and macro structures can be unified into a single coherent framework; (3) paragraph-level leaf nodes are appropriate for macro analysis; (4) primary-secondary relationships depend on discourse relation types; (5) MCDTB (97 annotated articles) demonstrates feasibility; (6) preliminary experiments validate the schema. As a claim verifier, I assess the evidence supporting each claim and identify gaps between assertions and supporting evidence. The paper's reasoning chain is logically coherent but exhibits significant evidentiary gaps: the 'neglect' claim relies on characterization rather than systematic literature review; the unification is presented as a design choice without formal theoretical justification; paragraph-level granularity is asserted but not empirically validated; the observed dependence between discourse relation types and primary-secondary relationships may reflect annotation design rather than linguistic structure (perfect correlations in Table 6); inter-annotator agreement metrics are referenced but not fully reported; and downstream task utility is claimed but not empirically demonstrated. The corpus contribution is concrete and the annotation schema is clearly described, but the theoretical and empirical foundations for the main claims require strengthening.

Micro-level (rhetorical/semantic) and macro-level (schematic/pragmatic) discourse structures are conceptually distinct but can be unified → a single coherent representation framework is feasible and valuable
Paragraph-level units are natural text segmentations in news discourse → they are appropriate leaf nodes for macro-level analysis (distinct from EDU-level micro analysis)
Discourse relation types show strong dependence on primary-secondary relationship types (Table 6: Joint→MP, Elaboration→P-S, Background→P-S) → this enables predictive modeling
MCDTB corpus (97 articles, 533 paragraphs, 438 relations) can be annotated using the unified schema → the schema is feasible to implement

Classification experiments on discourse relation and primary-secondary relation recognition achieve reasonable F-scores (57.1%-66.7% for relations, 50.0%-88.9% for primary-secondary) → the schema is appropriate for discourse structure analysis tasks
